notes: Line 93 gates extinction classification on `isExtinct && i > 10`, while the snapshot push (line 83) fires on isExtinct regardless of i. So extinction at loop index <=10 records an extinct snapshot but leaves status='completed'; the run stays 'completed' when the tick budget ends at/before i=11 or the dip is transient. The finding's 'runs to the end as completed' mechanism is only partly right (persistent extinction is caught at i=11 for longer runs), but the boundary misclassification genuinely holds.

compileExpression (lines 69-99) builds a strictly left-associative tree with no precedence: for [ref:population, op:>, val:10, kw:AND, ref:food, op:>, val:5] the trailing '>' at line 87-92 takes the whole {and:[{'>':[population,10]}, food]} as its left operand, yielding {'>':[{and:[...]},5]} exactly as claimed. Any rule mixing AND/OR with a following comparison compiles to wrong logic.

Lines 41 and 65 use String.replace with a string arg (first, unanchored occurrence). The startsWith(oldNamespace) guard checks a prefix while replace targets the first literal hit, so they disagree when oldNamespace is a short/common substring (e.g. 'a' vs 'abc/a_mod.json' -> 'bbc/a_mod.json'), corrupting move targets and manifest entries. The ref rewrite on line 9 correctly uses replaceAll anchored by '::', confirming the inconsistency.

JsonLogicAdapter.test.ts has three cases, all passing tokens:[] and a pre-built `compiled` object, so compileExpression's token-parsing body (atom/NOT consumption, AND/OR chaining, OP_MAP mapping, incomplete/empty error paths) is never exercised with real tokens. The precedence defect in R.run1.004 and any op-mapping regression would go uncaught.

HeadlessRunner.utils.test.ts covers only initializeWorldState (seed handling); runSimulationLoop (lines 69-104) has no test, leaving SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL cadence, the `isExtinct && i > 10` extinction classification, and the YIELD_INTERVAL await uncharacterized. Real gap on the loop that produces the status output, though it is diagnostic tooling.

walk resolves existing refs with existingIds.has(value) (exact, line 41) but flags broken refs with ENTITY_ID_PATTERN.test(value) (substring, line 52) and stores the whole string as missingId. A prose string containing a bare entity_ token (e.g. 'linked to entity_b') fails the exact match, passes the substring test, and survives the final filter at referenceIndex.ts:65 (which re-checks the whole string, not the extracted id), producing a false broken-reference; the exact-match half also misses ids embedded in larger strings.
